prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” agent for Pleasanton — the best person depends on your home, neighborhood, timeline and priorities — but I can help you find the right top-performing agent and give you a step-by-step plan to choose confidently.

Quick plan and what to do next
- Tell me your address or the neighborhood, target timeline, and any priorities (highest price, fastest sale, lowest commission, handling probate/tenant-occupied, etc.). I can then help short‑list agents or draft interview messages.
- If you already have candidate names, share them and I’ll help you compare.

How to identify the best agents for your home (practical criteria)
1. Proven track record in your immediate neighborhood or similar properties
   - Look for recent listings and closed sales of houses like yours (size, style, price range) in Pleasanton.
   - Check list price vs. sale price and days on market.

2. Seller-side experience (not just buyer leads)
   - Prefer agents who regularly represent sellers, ideally with multiple recent seller-side closings.

3. Marketing & presentation
   - Professional photography, floor plan, virtual tour, targeted online ad spend, brokerage syndication, print materials, and open-house strategy.

4. Pricing strategy & local market knowledge
   - Will provide a detailed CMA and explain comparable selection and pricing strategy for Pleasanton micro‑markets (e.g., West Pleasanton vs. Downtown).

5. Communication & responsiveness
   - Clear plan for how often and by what method they’ll update you; availability for showings and negotiations.

6. References & reviews
   - Ask for 2–3 recent seller references and verify online reviews (Google, Yelp, Zillow/Realtor profiles, Nextdoor).

7. Fees, net sheets and contract terms
   - Get a written net‑proceeds estimate, and understand commission, any marketing fees, and exclusive listing terms.

Where to search for candidates
- Zillow, Redfin, Realtor.com and local MLS listings for “sold” data.
- Google Business and Yelp for reviews.
- Local Facebook/Nextdoor groups and the Pleasanton Weekly classifieds.
- Ask neighbors who recently sold — neighborhood referrals are often the most relevant.

Important interview questions to ask each agent
- How many homes like mine have you sold in the past 12 months in Pleasanton? Can you show MLS examples?
- What was the list price vs. sale price and days on market for those sales?
- What is your recommended list price range and why?
- What concrete marketing steps will you take? (photos, staging, ads, open houses, broker tours)
- Who will be my day‑to‑day contact — you or a team member?
- How will you handle showings and feedback?
- What are your fees and contract length? Any cancellation provisions?
- Can I see references from recent seller clients?

Other practical tips
- Get at least 3 interviews/CMAs from different brokerages (including a top local solo agent and a team).
- Ask for a seller net sheet showing probable closing costs and net proceeds at different price points.
- Consider a pre-listing inspection and decluttering/staging to reduce surprises and speed sale.
- If you want top price, be prepared to allow professional marketing and possibly a flexible showing schedule.

If you want, provide:
- Your property address or neighborhood
- Target timeline and priorities
I’ll pull together a short checklist and a starter list of questions tailored to your house, or help evaluate specific agents you name.
